originality_rule: Techniques are LEARNED; drawings are ORIGINAL. No artwork traced, reproduced, or closely derived; per-entry notes state what is taken.

entries.observed: Guilloché defined as precise, intricate, repetitive patterns mechanically engraved via engine turning; the pattern family is the mathematical roulette (Spirograph) curves.
entries.idea_contributed: The whole complexity register the mandate asks for: dense families of parametric roulette curves whose precision visibly cannot be hand-faked — directly implementable as hypotrochoid ring stacks in two inks.
entries.originality_note: Technique class only; no plate or dial design copied.

entries.observed: Two machine families: the rose-engine lathe (rocking rosette discs, radial/lobed patterns) and the straight-line engine (parallel/lattice patterns).
entries.idea_contributed: Two distinct pattern SYSTEMS that can interact on one lid: a radial rosette system over a linear lattice system — exactly the >=2-interacting-systems bar.

entries.technique: rosette-disc rocking — wave imparted per revolution
entries.observed: Headstock rocks against a rosette disc whose perimeter carries a wave/scallop; as the work rotates the cut acquires that wave — producing scrolls, basket-weaves, sunbursts, moiré, barleycorn.
entries.idea_contributed: The generative rule r(θ) = base·(1 + depth·cos(lobes·θ + phase)) per ring, phase-stepped ring to ring — the exact construction used for our rosettes and bosses.
entries.originality_note: Formula-level idea; no specific rosette copied.

entries.technique: straight-line engine — basket weave, straight barley
entries.observed: The straight-line engine (planer-like) produces parallel or lattice patterns such as basket-weave and straight barley.
entries.idea_contributed: The orthogonal wave-lattice ground: rows and columns of phase-drifting sine lines interfering into a barleycorn field — a full-lid patterned GROUND under a foreground ornament (the depth bar).

entries.observed: A canon of named dial styles every enthusiast should know — waves, barleycorn, hobnail, sunburst, basket weave and others — each a distinct parametric family.
entries.idea_contributed: Style-diversity insurance: the five candidates should draw from DIFFERENT named families rather than five variants of one, so the board reads as a range of crafts.

entries.technique: métier attribution — which engine makes which pattern
entries.observed: Waves, barleycorn, flinqué, moiré come off the rose engine; clous de Paris, sunburst, basketweave off the straight-line engine.
entries.idea_contributed: Moiré is itself a recognized guilloché family — licenses the offset-ring moiré medallion as heritage craft, not a digital gimmick.

entries.observed: A generator whose computePoint produces spirograph coordinates, then displaces each point in polar coordinates by user-controlled amplitude/frequency/phase/exponent; exports SVG.
entries.idea_contributed: The two-stage construction — base curve family, then a second modulation applied over it — is the cleanest formal definition of 'two interacting pattern systems' and drives C1/C4's modulated rings.
entries.originality_note: Construction pipeline idea; our code is written fresh, no repo code or output copied.

entries.observed: A tutorial genre: security seals assembled from layered guilloché rosettes, borders and rules.
entries.idea_contributed: Assembly grammar — rosette + border + micro-rule layers composing one seal — informs C4's lattice-plus-centre-plus-border three-layer build.
entries.originality_note: Assembly grammar only; the tutorial's seal is not reproduced.

entries.observed: A working security-document/guilloché designer's practice page — the craft is a live professional discipline, not just heritage.
entries.idea_contributed: Confidence that banknote-grammar ornament reads as high-value print craft — the exact 'cannot be done easily' signal §L demands.
entries.originality_note: No portfolio piece viewed in detail or imitated.

entries.observed: The genre artifact: a many-lobed layered guilloché rosette offered for security-paper use.
entries.idea_contributed: Genre confirmation for a centre rosette of MANY interleaved lobed rings (not three or four) — ring count is where the perceived-value lives.
entries.originality_note: Genre observed; the stock asset itself is neither downloaded nor derived from.

entries.observed: Copperplate engraving reproduces ONLY linear marks; all tone is built from line.
entries.idea_contributed: The binding constraint that makes two-ink complexity honest: every 'shade' on the lid must be constructed from line weight, spacing, or density — never a third colour. Same law as our spot-ink discipline.

entries.observed: Equidistant roughly-parallel line sets form hatching; two intersecting sets form cross-hatching.
entries.idea_contributed: Cross-hatch as a legitimate second system over any motif — e.g. hatched fills inside cartouche spandrels or border reserves.

entries.observed: Contour hatching curves the hatch lines to follow three-dimensional volume rather than running straight.
entries.idea_contributed: Curved hatch families that follow a form's flow — usable to give a flat two-ink ornament an engraved, volumetric read (e.g. rings whose local spacing tightens toward edges).

entries.observed: Botanical hatching uses contour lines as guides so strokes flow with the form (e.g. curved verticals down a poppy seed head).
entries.idea_contributed: If a botanical motif appears, its interior tone should be flow-following hatch lines, not solid fill — the engraved-plate look in spot ink.

entries.observed: Image-based portrait engraving research: engraving-style line fields computed algorithmically from an underlying image/density.
entries.idea_contributed: Formal license for C2's move — a computed density field (glyph mask) steering a mechanical mark system (phyllotaxis dots) is the same idea class as computed engraving.
entries.originality_note: Idea class only; no algorithm or figure reproduced.

entries.observed: Victorian powder boxes carried floral trailing borders around the full circumference — leaves specked with three-petaled flowers — and designs enclosed within continuous arches bordered by button-shaped flowers.
entries.idea_contributed: The genre's own answer to a big plain lid: a continuous ornamental circuit (trailing border / arch arcade) enclosing the field — informs the braid/garland circuit and arch-thinking on a 72mm square.
entries.originality_note: Genre convention only; no box's artwork traced.

entries.observed: A board dedicated to Islamic-style girih decoration and strapwork — interlaced band ornament as a whole decorative language.
entries.idea_contributed: Strapwork as BANDS (double-edged straps) rather than single strokes — every interlace in round 2 is drawn as a two-edge band with real width.
entries.originality_note: Language only; no pinned design copied.

entries.observed: Islamic pattern education built on compass/straightedge constructions from grid intersections.
entries.idea_contributed: Constructive honesty: patterns derived from an underlying grid geometry (not freehand placement) — our lattices all derive from pitch grids with derived intersections.

entries.technique: algorithmic Islamic star patterns + consistent interlace
entries.observed: Kaplan's work on algorithmic construction of Islamic star patterns; strands drawn with consistent interlacing, passing alternately over and under at intersections.
entries.idea_contributed: The over-under CONSISTENCY rule: alternation must be maintained along each strand, which is why C3/C5 compute crossing parity instead of decorating gaps arbitrarily.

entries.observed: Construction walk-throughs for 8/12-point stars; the octagram (khatam) family tiles into star-and-cross fields.
entries.idea_contributed: The khatam two-square star as a tileable unit whose negative space forms crosses/octagons — C5's lattice cell.

entries.observed: Vogel (1979): r = c√n, φ = n·137.5°; consecutive-Fibonacci spiral arm counts emerge from the golden angle.
entries.idea_contributed: The exact dot-placement law for C2 — thousands of points, zero randomness, visible Fibonacci arm structure that reads as deep craft.

entries.observed: Phyllotaxis presented as a generative-art staple: golden angle + √n radius generating sunflower-like fields.
entries.idea_contributed: Confirmation the field is beautiful at print scale, and that modulating dot SIZE over the field (not position) is where art direction enters.

entries.observed: Moiré as interference between two nearly-identical repetitive patterns; concentric-circle pairs yield radiating interference arcs.
entries.idea_contributed: The offset twin-ring medallion (C3): two identical fine ring systems, centres a hair apart — interference arcs the eye cannot decompose, from two trivially-specified systems.

entries.observed: Programming exercise: overlaid animated concentric-circle generators create moiré line families radiating from near-centre.
entries.idea_contributed: Practical parameters — ring pitch and centre offset control the interference wavelength; informs choosing 0.016·FW offset at 0.008·FW pitch so arcs read at 72mm.

entries.observed: Embossing/debossing of logos or patterns adds a three-dimensional element that signals meticulous craftsmanship.
entries.idea_contributed: The eventual print destiny of these line systems: fine two-ink guilloché translates naturally to emboss/deboss plates — worth noting in the register for the print-shop spec later (owner-side, non-gating).

entries.observed: Heritage patterns (e.g. Catkin x Summer Palace embroidery-inspired designs) and metallic-embossed intricate floral motifs cited as luxury signals.
entries.idea_contributed: Heritage-technique storytelling IS the luxury cue — naming the technique per candidate on the contact sheet (engine-turned, strapwork, phyllotaxis…) lets the owner buy a craft, not just a picture.
entries.originality_note: Strategy only; no cited brand's artwork used.

entries.observed: Current-year luxury cosmetic packaging examples roundup — the register the FB3093 lid competes in.
entries.idea_contributed: Calibration that intricate pattern-forward lids are current, not costume — the mandate's 'more creativity' can be heritage-technical without reading dated.
